No slides, notes or gifts were found for Radiological examinations of the heart. This page gathers the imaging content that appears in the cardiac-surgery slide file (black) and adds a short orientation to cardiac imaging (added boxes). If you receive this lecture's slides, send them and the page will be rebuilt.

1. Imaging in the cardiac work-up (from the slides)

  • Approach to a cardiac patient: history → examination → chest X-ray → ECG → investigations.
  • Chest pain work-up: history & examination · X-ray chest, stress ECG · myocardial perfusion imaging · dobutamine stress echo · multislice CT with contrast · coronary angiography.
  • Pre-operative investigations for cardiac surgery: FBC, biochemistry, ECG, chest X-ray, PFTs, carotid duplex, peripheral duplex as needed, echocardiography, coronary angiography.
  • Pericardial effusion: plain chest X-ray, echocardiography, CT.
  • Cardiac tumours: echocardiography, CT, MRI.
  • Blunt cardiac trauma: exam, CXR, ECG, cardiac enzymes; echo, CT as needed.
  • Aortic dissection vs MI: wide mediastinum on the chest X-ray.

2. Chest X-ray signs on the slides

Added explanationReading a cardiac CXR (added): cardiothoracic ratio > 0.5 on a PA film = cardiomegaly · LA enlargement: straightened left heart border, double right-heart contour, splayed carina, elevated left main bronchus (MS) · LV enlargement: apex displaced down and out (AR, MR) · pulmonary venous congestion: upper-lobe diversion → Kerley B lines → bat-wing oedema, effusions · valve or annular calcification, prosthetic valves, sternal wires · widened mediastinum (dissection, aneurysm).

3. Other cardiac imaging (added)

Added explanationEchocardiography (TTE/TOE): the key test for valves (area, gradients, regurgitation), LV function (EF), wall motion, pericardial effusion/tamponade, vegetations (TOE more sensitive), intracardiac masses/thrombus (LA appendage on TOE). Stress echo (exercise or dobutamine) shows inducible ischaemia and viability.
Added explanationCoronary angiography: gold standard for coronary anatomy before PCI/CABG. CT coronary angiography (multislice CT): non-invasive for low–intermediate-risk chest pain; also CT angiography of the aorta for dissection/aneurysm. Cardiac MRI: function, viability (late gadolinium enhancement), cardiomyopathy, tumours, congenital disease. Nuclear perfusion imaging (SPECT/PET): ischaemia and viability.
